about: Major deserts at their present-day extent, painted in the same sand as the Sahara. The Sahara itself is NOT here: it has its own field and its own Green Sahara toggle.

sourced.extent: Natural Earth 10m geography regions (public domain); the named polygons in each field, unedited.
sourced.margin_fade: Beyer, R.M., Krapp, M. & Manica, A. (2020). High-resolution terrestrial climate, bioclimate and vegetation for the last 120,000 years. Scientific Data 7, 236. doi:10.1038/s41597-020-0552-1. CC BY 4.0. Present-day BIOME4 class at 0.5 degrees, used to weight each cell so that semi-arid ground inside a generous polygon is not painted as sand.

drawn: The 0.6 degree blur on every edge, and the weights given to the part-desert biome classes: 12=0.15, 13=0.45, 14=0.45, 19=0.25, 20=0.30, 21=1.00, 27=0.75, with a floor of 0.12 inside the polygon. A drawing, not a reconstruction.
not_drawn: The Sahara (its own field). Dune fields are not distinguished from stony desert. The Central Asian and Iranian deserts (Garagum, Qizilqum, Betpaqdala, Kavir, Lut, Margo, Rigestan), the Danakil, the Chalbi, the Negev and the Caatingas are in the source and are not drawn, because the ruling named nine regions and these are not among them. The Mojave is not drawn because Natural Earth has no Mojave polygon.

fields.label: The American Southwest and the Great Basin
